newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks rally on weak retail sales data.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks rally on weak retail sales data.

text.p: Stocks soared Thursday as weak May U.S. retail sales data helped blue-chips rise further into record territory.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 84.11 at 7,659.94 after setting records in the last four sessions. Advancing issues led declines two-to-one in active trading of 332 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts said weaker-than-expected retail sales data prompted a bond market rally that, in turn, boosted blue-chip stocks.
High-technology stocks, however, largely faltered, and the technology-laden Nasdaq composite index was off 0.30 at 1,407.55.
"The market is making new highs but the technology sector is not part of the picture," said Arun Kumar, equities strategist at Lehman Brothers.

Analysts said technology stocks were pressured by declines in computer chip powerhouse Intel Corp., whose stock fell 3-1/2 to 144. Goldman Sachs cut its 1997 earnings estimates for Intel while Cowen & Co. lowered its recommendation on Intel to neutral from buy.
The Commerce Department reported that U.S. May retail sales dropped 0.1 percent to a seasonally adjusted $210.3 billion after revised drops of 0.9 percent in April and 0.3 percent in March.
Wall Street economists had expected May sales to increase 0.4 percent.
Jobless claims for the week ended June 7 edged up to 339,000. Economists had expected the claims number to fall.
The combined data, which suggests a slowdown in economic activity, made investors more confident that the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates when it meets in early July.
Peggy Farley, managing director of Amas Securities Inc., said the figures were a "good Fed comforter."
Analysts said it was the first time in more than 15 years that retail sales have weakened for three months in a row.
The benchmark 30-year bond rose 29/32, or $9.06 per $1,000 face value, lowering its yield to 6.77 percent from 6.84 percent on Wednesday.

Hildegard Zagorski, market analyst at Prudential Securities, said the stock market strength could be seen in several sectors, including banks, financial stocks as well as cyclical stocks like pulp and paper.
Weyerhaeuser Co. gained 7/8 to 54-1/4 and International Paper Co. rose 1 to 51-3/8.
Polo Ralph Lauren strode into the market with a 5-1/4 gain, rising to 31-1/4, in its stock market debut. The design house's shares jumped about 25 percent at the opening of trading.

Philip Morris shares gained 2-1/4 to 44-7/8. The company was leading the tobacco industry's challenge to a Massachusetts law that requires the disclosure of cigarette ingredients to state health authorities.
The American Stock Exchange index was up 1.83 at 624.50, and the Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 8.14 points to 877.71.
